subject: General Aptitude
summary: percentages, ratio and proportion, averages, profit and loss, time-speed-distance (trains, boats, races) and time and work (pipes, efficiency, man-days)

questions.text: A's monthly income is 25 % less than B's. By what percentage is B's income more than A's?
solution: Concept: Percentage change is always measured on the base you compare against.
Let B = 100, then A = 75. B exceeds A by 25 on a base of 75.
Exam tip: If A is r % less than B, then B is r/(100 − r) × 100 % more than A. Memorise the pairs 20 ↔ 25, 25 ↔ 33.33, 50 ↔ 100.

questions.text: The price of an item is first increased by 10 % and then decreased by 20 %. The net percentage change in its price is (enter a negative number for a decrease) ______
solution: Concept: Successive changes multiply: net factor = (1 + a/100)(1 + b/100).
Net change = -12 % (a 12 % decrease)
Exam tip: Shortcut a + b + ab/100 = 10 − 20 − 2 = −12. The order of the changes does not matter.

questions.text: ₹7800 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4. A's share is
solution: Concept: Clear fractional ratios by multiplying every term by the LCM of the denominators.

questions.text: The average of 11 results is 60. The average of the first six results is 58 and that of the last six is 63. The sixth result is ______
solution: Concept: The sixth result is counted in both groups, so adding the two group-sums counts it twice.
Sum of all 11 = 660; first six = 348; last six = 378
Exam tip: Overlap problems: (sum of groups) − (total) = the overlapped item(s).

questions.text: A batsman's average after 10 innings is 32. How many runs must he score in the 11th innings to raise his average to 36? ______
solution: Concept: Work with totals, not averages.
Total after 10 innings = 320; required total after 11 = 11 × 36 = 396
Runs needed = 396 − 320 = 76
Exam tip: Shortcut: new score = new average + (number of old innings × rise) = 36 + 10 × 4 = 76.

questions.text: An article costs ₹800. The shopkeeper wants a 15 % profit after allowing an 8 % discount on the marked price. The marked price must be
solution: Concept: SP = CP(1 + profit %) = MP(1 − discount %).
Exam tip: MP/CP = (1 + p)/(1 − d) = 1.15/0.92 = 1.25: mark the article 25 % above cost.

questions.text: A dishonest dealer claims to sell at cost price but uses a weight of 800 g instead of 1 kg. His gain percentage is ______
solution: Concept: Gain % = (true weight − false weight)/false weight × 100.
He gives goods costing ₹800 but charges ₹1000.
Exam tip: Divide by the false weight (800), not the true weight (1000). That trap gives the common wrong answer 20 %.

questions.text: A train passes a pole in 15 seconds and a 100 m long platform in 25 seconds. The length of the train (in metres) is ______
solution: Concept: Passing a pole: distance = train length; passing a platform: distance = train length + platform length.
The extra 10 s is spent covering the 100 m platform, so speed = 100/10 = 10 m/s
Exam tip: Speed = 10 m/s = 36 km/h. Multiply m/s by 18/5 to convert to km/h.

questions.text: Two cars start at the same time from towns P and Q, 300 km apart, and drive towards each other at 40 km/h and 60 km/h respectively. The distance of their meeting point from P (in km) is ______
solution: Concept: Moving towards each other, the gap closes at the sum of the speeds.
Time to meet = 300/(40 + 60) = 3 h
Distance from P = 40 × 3 = 120 km
Exam tip: The meeting point divides the distance in the ratio of the speeds, 40 : 60 = 2 : 3, so 2/5 × 300 = 120 km without finding the time.

questions.text: A boat's speed in still water is 8 km/h and the stream flows at 2 km/h. The time taken to go 30 km downstream and come back is
solution: Concept: Downstream speed = b + s, upstream speed = b − s.
Downstream: 30/10 = 3 h; upstream: 30/6 = 5 h
Total = 8 h
Exam tip: 30 × 2/8 = 7.5 h is the answer in still water: a current always lengthens a round trip.

questions.text: 12 men can complete a work in 18 days. They work for 6 days, and then 4 more men join them. The number of days needed to finish the remaining work is ______
solution: Concept: Use man-days: work = men × days.
Total work = 12 × 18 = 216 man-days; done in 6 days = 72 man-days
Remaining 144 man-days with 16 men: 144/16 = 9 days
Exam tip: Total time = 6 + 9 = 15 days. Man-day accounting avoids fractions completely.

questions.text: A is twice as efficient as B. Working together they finish a job in 14 days. The number of days A alone would take is ______
solution: Concept: Efficiency is the work done per day; time is inversely proportional to efficiency.
Let B's rate = x, A's rate = 2x. 3x × 14 = 1 → x = 1/42
B alone: 42 days; A alone (twice as fast): 21 days
Exam tip: Ratio of rates 2 : 1, so A does 2/3 of the work in 14 days; the whole work takes A 14 × 3/2 = 21 days.

questions.text: A pipe can fill a tank in 6 hours. Because of a leak at the bottom, it takes 8 hours to fill the tank. The leak alone can empty the full tank in
solution: Concept: Net rate = filling rate − leak rate.
Leak rate = 1/6 − 1/8 = (4 − 3)/24 = 1/24 of the tank per hour
Leak empties the tank in 24 h
Exam tip: Shortcut: ab/(b − a) = 6 × 8/(8 − 6) = 24 h.

questions.text: A 40-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much water (in litres) must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2? ______
solution: Concept: The quantity that does not change (milk) fixes the new total.
Milk = 30 L, water = 10 L.
Exam tip: Always anchor on the unchanged component; never scale the whole mixture.

questions.text: In a 200 m race, A beats B by 20 m and A beats C by 38 m. In a 200 m race between B and C, B beats C by (in metres) ______
solution: Concept: In the same time the distances run are in the ratio of the speeds.
When A runs 200 m: B runs 180 m and C runs 162 m. So B : C = 180 : 162 = 10 : 9.
When B runs 200 m, C runs 200 × 9/10 = 180 m: B wins by 20 m
Exam tip: Not 38 − 20 = 18 m: the margins come from different race lengths, so use speed ratios.
